summary:
Global investment firm Norwest Venture Partners has offloaded a 2.15% stake in SaaS company Amagi through a block deal worth Rs 262.44 crore. 
According to exchange data, Norwest Venture Partners X Mauritius sold 47.37 lakh shares at Rs 554 each on the NSE. The transaction was executed at a discount of around 3% to Amagi's previous closing price of Rs 571.05 per share. 
On the buying side, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund acquired 33.27 lakh shares worth Rs 184.33 crore. Old Bridge Capital Management's All Cap Strategy picked up 7.65 lakh shares worth Rs 42.38 crore, while Long Term Equity Fund acquired 6.45 lakh shares worth Rs 35.73 crore. All the transactions took place at Rs 554 per share.
Norwest Venture Partners held an 11.76% stake in Amagi as of September 2026. Following the latest transaction, its shareholding is expected to decline to around 9.61%.
Amagi recently reported a strong performance in the second quarter of FY27. Its operating revenue grew 27% year-on-year to Rs 476 crore. The company's profit after tax surged nearly 30-fold to Rs 75 crore during the quarter. 
Following the transaction, shares of the company ended Thursday's trading session at Rs 582.80, giving the company total market capitalization of Rs 12,831 crore or $1.35 billion.

title: Namma Yatri's revenue grows 89% to Rs 37.5 Cr in FY26; losses narrow 15%
summary:
Namma Yatri entered the ride-hailing market in 2022 as an auto-rickshaw booking platform. It adopted a different approach in a segment dominated by Uber, Rapido and Ola. The Bengaluru-based company reported an 89.4% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY26, while its losses narrowed by nearly 15% during the same period.
Namma Yatri's revenue from operations rose to Rs 37.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 19.8 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Unlike the conventional commission-based model, Namma Yatri introduced a zero-commission model for drivers, allowing them to retain the entire fare paid by customers. Instead, the company earns through fixed subscription fees or per-trip charges for using its platform.

It also earned Rs 2 crore from gains on the sale of investments, taking its total income to Rs 39.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 23.5 crore in FY25.
On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost centre, accounting for around 41% of its total expenditure. The expense increased 12.7% to Rs 34.5 crore in FY26. Advertising and promotional expenses also saw a 38% jump to Rs 16.7 crore during the year.
Other expenses, including legal, information technology, field operations, telecalling, recruitment and travel, pushed the company's overall expenditure up 11.2% to Rs 83.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 74.9 crore in FY25.
Despite the sharp growth in revenue, Namma Yatri continues to spend considerably more than it earns from operations. However, slower growth in expenses helped the company bring down its net loss by 14.8% to Rs 43.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 51.4 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 2.22 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at 79.8% and 106%, respectively.
The ride-hailing space has become increasingly competitive, with Rapido making strong inroads into autos and cab services, while Ola and Uber continue to hold a sizeable presence. Namma Yatri's zero-commission model gave it a different identity when it entered the market, but standing out is no longer enough. The company will have to bring more drivers and customers onto its platform while keeping costs under control. Its FY26 numbers show that revenue is growing, but getting the business to profitability remains a much bigger task.

title: Nexent Capital launches $1 Bn fund for AI infra, advanced energy investments
summary:
Nexent Capital IFSC has launched Nexent Capital ADGM Fund I, a closed-end fund targeting $1 billion in capital commitments, with the corpus expandable to $1.6 billion. The fund will focus on quantum-ready AI infrastructure and advanced energy investments.
The fund is structured as an Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM)-domiciled Qualified Investor Fund (QIF), with a GIFT City-based, IFSCA-regulated Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) serving as its feeder vehicle. Nexent Capital ADGM Limited is being established as the fund manager.
The fund has secured an anchor commitment of $20 million from the Tyagi family office. It has also identified a pipeline of AI infrastructure and advanced energy projects across North America and India. These include data centre and power assets sponsored by affiliates of the Nexent Capital and Tryfacta platforms.
Nexent Capital ADGM Fund I will deploy capital across five investment strategies: infrastructure private equity in AI and data centre assets, private credit and structured capital, special-situations mergers and acquisitions (M&A), growth equity and private investment in public equity (PIPEs), and liquid public equity exposure across the AI and data centre value chain.
Nexent Capital IFSC is working with an Abu Dhabi-based fund administrator that manages more than $3.4 trillion in assets globally. It is also progressing the formal appointment of legal counsel and an auditor as part of its process to secure Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) authorisation and achieve the fund’s first close.
The fund has a minimum investment commitment of $500,000. It is targeting its first close within approximately six months of receiving FSRA authorisation, followed by a final close six months later.
The launch comes amid growing investor interest in infrastructure supporting AI deployment, including power generation, data centres and advanced energy systems. GIFT City and ADGM are also emerging as gateways for cross-border alternative investment structures.
Nexent Capital is a financial services firm focused on investment banking, financial advisory, alternative asset management and institutional equities. It has offices in San Francisco, California, and GIFT City, Gujarat.

title: Uber appoints former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan as India president
summary:
Uber has appointed former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan as president for India and South Asia. 
He will take charge from January 4, 2027, and report to Dom Taylor, Uber’s regional general manager for Asia Pacific.
The appointment follows the departure of Uber India and South Asia President Prabhjeet Singh after spending nearly 11 years with the ride hailing company.
Ranjan will join Uber from edtech company Allen Online, where he is currently the CEO. He spent eight years at Zomato, joining the foodtech company in 2017. During his tenure, he held leadership roles across Zomato Gold, sales and its B2B business Hyperpure before becoming CEO of the food ordering and delivery business.
The appointment follows a search process spanning more than three months. Ranjan succeeds Prabhjeet Singh, who left Uber India in July after 11 years to join OpenAI as its India managing director.
Ranjan’s experience in running consumer businesses in India and his understanding of the market would help lead its next phase of growth in the region. His priorities include improving ride reliability, offering value across different journeys and creating better earning opportunities for drivers.
India is Uber’s third-largest market globally by trips, after the US and Brazil, and its second-largest market by number of earners. The company operates in more than 225 cities in the country, with over two million monthly active drivers earning through its platform.
Uber entered India in 2013 and has expanded its mobility services beyond cabs to include bikes, autos and metro services. The company is facing competition from players such as Rapido, particularly in price-sensitive mobility segments.
The leadership change comes as Uber looks to strengthen its position in India amid challenges related to driver supply, fuel costs and rider incentives. Earlier this year, the company infused Rs 2,921 crore into its India arm.

title: GIVA raises Rs 90 Cr from BlackSoil for retail expansion
summary:
Jewellery brand GIVA has raised Rs 90 crore in debt financing from alternative credit platform BlackSoil, its second fundraise in November.
The latest financing comes shortly after GIVA raised over $100 million in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management earlier this month.
According to the press release, the fresh capital will primarily be used to support store-level capital expenditure and working capital needs as the Bengaluru-based company expands its retail network and omnichannel operations.
Founded in 2019 by Ishendra Agarwal, GIVA started as a digital-first silver jewellery brand and has since diversified into gold jewellery and lab-grown diamonds. Its portfolio includes sterling silver, gold-plated, rose gold-plated, gold and diamond jewellery across categories for men, women and children.
The company operates through its direct-to-consumer platform, e-commerce and quick-commerce marketplaces, alongside an expanding offline network. GIVA currently has over 400 stores across more than 80 cities in India.

title: Kiwi spends Rs 105 Cr on ads; earns Rs 16 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
India's credit-on-UPI market has attracted several fintech startups looking to tap the growing adoption of digital payments and RuPay credit cards. Kiwi has built its business around this emerging opportunity, but monetising the model remains a challenge, with the startup generating just Rs 16 crore in operating revenue in FY26 despite spending heavily on customer acquisition and cashbacks.
Four years old Kiwi’s revenue from operations jumped over 4 times to Rs 16 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 3.8 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Launched in 2022, Kiwi offers RuPay credit cards in partnership with banks such as YES Bank, PNB and AU Small Finance Bank, allowing users to make UPI payments and earn cashback. It also offers Kiwi Postpaid, a bank-backed credit line that lets users make UPI payments even with zero account balance and repay the dues through a monthly billing cycle.

The company follows a partnership-led revenue model, earning through revenue-sharing arrangements with banks on card distribution and transaction volumes, alongside potential income from premium memberships and platform fees.
Sale of the above-mentioned service was the source of revenue for the firm in FY26. However, it also earned Rs 8.9 crore through interest on fixed deposits and sale of mutual funds that pushed its overall income to Rs 24.9 crore during the last fiscal year.
Advertising and promotional expenses remained Kiwi's largest cost centre, potentially covering customer acquisition campaigns, cashback and other promotional incentives. The expense surged 2.7X to Rs 105 crore in FY26 from Rs 38.5 crore in the previous fiscal year, accounting for 68% of the company's total expenditure.
Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses increased 15.6% to Rs 26.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 22.75 crore in FY25. This included Rs 5.8 crore in ESOP-related expenses.
However, its total expenses more than doubled to Rs 154.5 crore during the fiscal year from Rs 73.8 crore in FY25. The increase was largely driven by advertising and promotional expenses, which emerged as the company's biggest cost centre.
Software expenses doubled to Rs 12 crore. Legal and professional expenses stood at Rs 5 crore, compared with Rs 4 crore in FY25. Other expenses, including payment gateway charges, travelling expenses, depreciation & amortization collectively added Rs 11.2 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Overall expenditure for the Nexus Venture Partners-backed firm doubled to Rs 154.5 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 73.8 crore in FY25.
The sharp increase in advertising and promotional expenses weighed on Kiwi's bottom line, which doubled its losses to Rs 129.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 64.2 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Kiwi reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 138 crore in FY26, while its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at -86.94% and -863.13%, respectively. At a unit level, the Bengaluru-based startup spent Rs 9.66 for every rupee of operating revenue earned.

Kiwi has raised around $43 million to date, including a $24 million Series B round in September last year. The round was led by Vertex Ventures, with participation from existing investors Nexus Venture Partners, Stellaris Venture Partners and Omidyar Network.
Following the allotment of shares in the latest round, Nexus Venture Partners emerged as the largest shareholder with a 21.06% stake, followed by Stellaris Venture Partners at 15.47%. New investor Vertex Ventures holds 13%, while co-founders Siddharth Mehta, Anup Kumar Agrawal and Mohit Bedi collectively own 35.48% of the company.

title: Zostel moves Delhi HC to revive 7% stake claim in OYO parent
summary:
Zostel has approached the Delhi High Court seeking to revive its claim to a 7% stake in Oravel Stays, OYO's parent company, as it moves towards a proposed IPO.
The company has challenged a May 2025 order that set aside a 2021 arbitral award recognising its entitlement to the stake following a proposed acquisition of its hotel aggregation business, Zo Rooms, in 2015.
During Wednesday's hearing, Zostel argued that the court should have set aside only the relief granted by the arbitrator rather than the entire award. It maintained that the tribunal's findings on the binding nature of the deal and Oravel's alleged breach should have been retained.
The dispute dates back to November 2015, when Oravel and Zostel signed a term sheet for the acquisition of Zo Rooms. Under the proposed deal, Zostel's shareholders were to receive a 7% stake in Oravel. Although the term sheet was described as non-binding, Zostel argued that subsequent actions by both parties made it binding. The final agreements were never signed.
In 2021, an arbitral tribunal ruled in Zostel's favour. However, the Delhi High Court set aside the award in May 2025, citing a lack of clarity around the specific performance granted by the arbitrator.
During Wednesday's hearing, the division bench questioned whether specific performance could be directed when the final agreements had never been executed. The outcome of the appeal could determine whether Zostel's 7% stake claim is revived.

title: Orthopaedic healthcare startup OSSO raises Rs 2.5 Cr in extended seed round
summary:
Gurugram-based orthopaedic healthcare startup OSSO has raised Rs 2.5 crore as part of its extended seed funding round.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its clinical capabilities and presence across the National Capital Region (NCR), OSSO said in a press release.
The extended round saw participation from Rajeev Saraf, Tejinderpal Miglani, Priyanka Aggarwal, Akshay Varma and Vikas Bhadoria. They join existing investors, including Umesh Kumar Agarwal from the Haldiram Family Office, Sahil Jindal and Blume Founders Fund, among others.
Founded in 2025 by Kunal Kishore Dhawan and Avani Shukla, OSSO operates an integrated orthopaedic and rehabilitation centre that combines clinical orthopaedics, physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R), physiotherapy, regenerative orthopaedics and sports injury care.
The startup's newly launched centre will focus on advanced orthopaedic procedures, particularly joint preservation and sports injury treatment.
The facility will offer procedures such as image-guided orthobiologic interventions, subchondral bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) and arthroscopic cartilage repair. Several of these treatments are minimally invasive and can be performed as day-care procedures.
The new centre will operate alongside OSSO's flagship clinic in DLF Phase 4, Gurugram. This will allow the startup to integrate patient care across diagnosis, procedures and rehabilitation.
OSSO plans to expand its presence across NCR in 2027, with five to six additional clinics and surgical units. It also plans to onboard more orthopaedic surgeons as it builds a doctor-led platform focused on orthopaedic care.
The startup aims to build a network that brings specialised clinical services, surgical capabilities and rehabilitation under one platform.

title: Libas’ revenue grows 19% to Rs 726 Cr in FY26; losses narrow marginally
summary:
India’s ethnic wear market is seeing growing competition from established brands such as Biba, Manyavar and Fabindia, alongside newer labels targeting demand for contemporary ethnic and fusion wear. Players such as Libas are building an omnichannel presence with traditional designs and affordable pricing, as online shopping and organised retail open up opportunities beyond metro cities. However, rising competition and sourcing, marketing and distribution costs remain key challenges.
Against this backdrop, Gurugram-based Libas continued to expand its business in the financial year ended March 2026, with revenue from operations growing 19% year-on-year to Rs 726 crore. However, the ethnic wear brand remained in the red, although its net losses narrowed marginally during the year, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 1985, Libas is a women's fashion brand offering ethnic and fusion wear, including kurtas, suits, sarees, lehengas, dresses and bottom wear. The brand caters to traditional and contemporary fashion preferences through its online platform and offline stores, with apparel sales remaining its sole source of revenue in FY26.
In terms of cost structure, cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense head, up 34.6% to Rs 426.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 316.9 crore in FY25. It accounted for around 57.4% of the company's total expenses.
Employee benefit expenses, the second-largest cost component, increased 53% to Rs 67.7 crore from Rs 44.3 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses also grew 17.9% to Rs 66 crore from Rs 56 crore.
Meanwhile, selling and distribution costs declined 20.2% to Rs 46.1 crore. Fabrication expenses, which cover costs related to garment stitching, processing and finishing, also fell 32.5% to Rs 40.35 crore during the year.
Other operating and administrative overheads such as rent, legal & professional, transportation and others also contributed to increase in overall expenses.
Consequently, Libas’ total expenses increased 19.6% to Rs 742.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 621.2 crore in FY25. The company reported a net loss of Rs 15.2 crore, a 7.9% improvement from Rs 16.5 crore in the previous fiscal. However, it remained EBITDA positive with an operating surplus of Rs 4 crore during the year.

The company’s Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stood at -9.04%, while its EBITDA margin was 0.55%. On a unit basis, Libas spent Rs 1.02 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. As of March 2026, it had total current assets of Rs 377.6 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 41.4 crore.
In May 2024, Libas raised Rs 150 crore ($18 million) from IAF Series 5, a fund managed by ICICI Venture, in its maiden external funding round.
Its competitors, Biba Fashion, reported revenue of around Rs 765 crore in FY25, while Vedant Fashions, the parent of Manyavar and Mohey, clocked revenue of Rs 1,436 crore in FY26.

title: Exclusive: Univest to raise Rs 75 Cr at Rs 1,500 Cr valuation
summary:
Stock market advisory platform Univest is in advanced talks to raise around Rs 75 crore (around $8 million) in a fresh funding round at a valuation of Rs 1,500 crore, according to sources familiar with the development.
“An undisclosed family office is leading the round, while Bertelsmann and stand up entertainer Zakir Khan are also participating,” sources told Entrackr.
The new round would value the company at nearly 2.4 times its previous post-money valuation of Rs 615 crore. Univest has achieved an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of around Rs 230 crore in November and is on track to turn PAT positive this month, sources added.
Co-founded in 2022 by Pranit Arora and Avneet Dhamija, Univest is a retail advisory platform that offers general recommendations through its SEBI-registered research analyst (RA) entity, Uniresearch. It provides trading advice across stocks, derivatives and commodities.
The startup raised $10 million in a Series A in December 2024, led by Bertelsmann India. In June 2025, it also concluded its first employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buyback worth Rs 1.61 crore.
Univest competes with several retail investment advisory platforms, including StockGrow, Liquide, Waya, TejiMandi, Stoxbox and INDmoney.
“The transaction is nearing completion, and if nothing goes wrong, the round will be announced soon,” sources said.
BII declined to comment on the story, while Univest did not respond to Entrackr’s queries until the time of publication. The story will be updated if the company responds.
While Univest has yet to file its annual financial statements for FY26, the firm reported Rs 41 crore revenue and Rs 31.84 crore loss in FY25.

A fresh funding round would be a vote of confidence in the firm and its future plans, which could include getting into wealth management directly perhaps. The subscription-based advisory business is obviously counting on a continuation of the rising trend of market participation by retail investors,  besides growing affluence of course. To that end, fund raises by a startup like Univest goes well beyond just a financial punt, and   is a broader bet on the Indian economy per se.

title: Flipkart confirms Kalyan Krishnamurthy’s exit after 11 years
summary:
Flipkart has confirmed that Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy is concluding his tenure at the Walmart-owned e-commerce company after more than 11 years.
The company said it will announce his successor in the coming weeks. In the interim, Balaji Thiagarajan, currently Chief Product and Technology Officer at Flipkart, and the Flipkart board will lead the organisation.
Krishnamurthy led Flipkart through a decade of growth, with the company’s business expanding more than fivefold during his leadership. He took charge of the company after founders Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal exited following Walmart’s acquisition of Flipkart in 2018.
During his tenure, Krishnamurthy oversaw Flipkart’s expansion across categories and geographies, while strengthening its position amid growing competition from Amazon and newer entrant Meesho. The company also expanded its quick commerce offering, Minutes, and built several consumer and seller-focused services.
Under his leadership, Flipkart’s Big Billion Days sale became a major part of India’s festive shopping season. The company also introduced several new initiatives and expanded its seller ecosystem.
“Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled and his many contributions to the company,” said Chris Nicholas, president and CEO of Walmart International.
Krishnamurthy said he was proud of the scale of the business and the way it had been built, adding that ethics, integrity and governance remained central to the company’s growth.
The development comes at a challenging time for Flipkart. The company has faced an IPO delay, fundraising efforts and a series of senior-level exits.

title: Prosus’ India ecosystem crosses 500 Mn users, PayU turns profitable in H1 FY27
summary:
Global technology investor Prosus said its India ecosystem has crossed 500 million annual users and is processing 450 million orders every month in the first half of FY27. Its fintech arm PayU also turned adjusted EBITDA-positive during the period.
According to the press release, the company reported ecosystem revenue of $5.7 billion for the six months ended September 2026, up 59% year-on-year. However, revenue growth stood at 10% in local currency, excluding the impact of acquisitions.
Prosus reported ecosystem adjusted EBITDA of $492 million, compared to $530 million in the corresponding period last year. This includes $344 million in investments in food delivery businesses iFood and Just Eat Takeaway (JET).
In India, PayU's revenue grew 6% in local currency, excluding acquisitions, to $384 million. Its adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $12 million, driven by growth in higher-margin services.
PayU's credit business was a key growth driver, with revenue rising 24% in reported currency to $119 million. Its credit assets under management grew 20%, while credit business EBITDA turned positive at $10 million. On the other hand, payments revenue declined 12% to $265 million.
The company said payment volumes processed by PayU across its ecosystem grew over 80% year-on-year. Its India portfolio also includes investments in companies such as Swiggy, Meesho, ixigo and Rapido.
Outside India, Prosus' food delivery investments continued to weigh on profitability. iFood's revenue grew 20% to $1.1 billion, but its adjusted EBITDA declined to $28 million from $184 million a year ago, reflecting an incremental investment of $278 million.
There was some improvement at JET (Just Eat Takeaway.com), which recorded order growth in September for the first time in 55 months. Its revenue declined 13% to $1.7 billion, the press release added.
Meanwhile, Prosus generated $1.1 billion in free cash flow and reported 12% growth in adjusted earnings per share.

title: Aeravti Ventures launches Rs 300 Cr Fund II, secures over 50% commitments at first close
summary:
Bengaluru-based venture capital firm Aeravti Ventures has launched its second fund with a target corpus of Rs 300 crore. The firm has secured commitments for more than half of the target corpus at the first close and expects to complete the final close within the next six months.
The SEBI-registered Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) will invest in 9-10 early-stage startups across three themes: food security, health infrastructure and physical security.
The fund will explore opportunities across agriculture, biosciences, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, waste management and energy. It will invest from pre-seed to pre-Series A stages, with a preference for leading pre-seed and seed rounds.
Aeravti Ventures II plans to write initial cheques of Rs 6-10 crore per company, with the capacity to invest two to three times the initial amount in follow-on rounds.
Shubham Jhuria, Partner and CFO at Aeravti Ventures, said participation from existing investors reflects the relationships and confidence built through the firm’s first fund.
Aeravti’s first fund achieved a final close of Rs 76 crore and has been fully deployed across seven companies. The firm led the seed round in each of them, while three portfolio companies are currently profitable.
Among its portfolio companies, Origin Fresh has grown its monthly revenue fourfold while maintaining profitability. ONO expanded its lending footprint before acquiring an NBFC licence, while East Ocyon has received positive feedback from its pre-clinical trials.
The firm has also added senior members, including Anam Ajani and Aditya Siroya, to strengthen its team.

title: Marico-owned Cosmix doubles revenue and profit in FY26
summary:
Multinational consumer goods company Marico acquired a 60% stake in Cosmix in February 2026 at Rs 375 crore. The acquisition comes as the digital-first nutrition brand nearly doubled its scale and bottom line during FY26.
Cosmix’s revenue from operations surged 95.74% to Rs 92 crore in FY26, up from Rs 47 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Founded in 2019, Cosmix operates as a digital-first nutrition and wellness brand with a focus on plant-based products. Its portfolio includes plant-based protein, multivitamins, superfoods, and other wellness products. The company primarily sells through its own website and online marketplaces. Sales of these products remained its sole source of revenue during FY26.

Like several other D2C brands, advertising and promotional expenses remained its largest cost centre, accounting for around 35% of the overall expenditure. This expense increased 85.7% to Rs 26 crore in FY26 from Rs 14 crore in the previous fiscal.
The cost of materials consumed also nearly doubled during the year, in line with the growth in business. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 5 crore, while freight, marketplace fees, finance costs, depreciation and other overheads pushed the company's total expenditure up 92% to Rs 75 crore in FY26 from Rs 39 crore in FY25.
Despite the increase in expenses, Cosmix managed to maintain its profitability as its net profit doubled to Rs 12.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 6 crore in FY25. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 0.82 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. Its EBITDA margin stood at 19%, while return on capital employed (ROCE) was 77.6%.

Cosmix's performance also reflects the growing maturity of India's D2C ecosystem, where several digital-first brands are scaling up while maintaining healthy profitability. Large FMCG players such as Marico and HUL have increasingly turned to acquisitions and strategic investments to strengthen their presence in emerging consumer categories. These companies are betting on brands that have already built a consumer base, established online distribution and demonstrated the potential to scale. With the backing of established players, these D2C brands could be better positioned to expand their distribution, reach more consumers and sustain growth in the coming years.
Marico has been expanding its D2C portfolio through acquisitions, which already includes plant-based nutrition brand Plix, True Elements, Just Herbs and men's grooming brand Beardo.
On the other hand, HUL has also been expanding its presence in the D2C space through acquisitions, including skincare brand Minimalist and nutrition brand OZiva. It had also picked up a minority stake in Wellbeing Nutrition before exiting the investment.

title: Shadowfax to acquire WeFast India assets, Borzo IP for Rs 23.3 Cr
summary:
Shadowfax Technologies has agreed to acquire select business assets of WeFast India and technology and intellectual property (IP) rights associated with Borzo for $2.5 million (approximately Rs 23.3 crore) as the logistics company expands into on-demand intra-city goods transportation.
The transaction involves two separate agreements. Shadowfax will acquire technology, software and related IP rights in India from Incrin Limited for $2 million, along with a licence for the BORZO trademark for $50,000.
Under a separate agreement, Shadowfax will purchase identified business assets of Wefast India Private Limited for $450,000 in Indian rupees. These include contracts, equipment, domain names, databases and related technology. The agreement also provides for the transfer of identified employees.
The transactions are subject to customary conditions precedent and are expected to be completed by March 31, 2027.
The deal will allow Shadowfax to extend its logistics services to small and medium businesses (SMEs) and customer-to-customer (C2C) deliveries, according to a press release.
Founded in Mumbai in 2016, WeFast operates across more than five cities. The company has over 32,000 delivery partners who complete more than 1.2 crore deliveries annually. It generated around Rs 200 crore in adjusted revenue in CY2025.
The transaction will give Shadowfax access to WeFast's existing network and customer base in the intra-city logistics segment. The company plans to combine its technology and delivery network with WeFast's operations to serve shop owners, distributors and individual users.

The penalties followed show-cause notices issued by the Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI), which alleged that Turtlemint had raised invoices on insurance companies without the actual supply of services. The company challenged these orders before the GST Appellate Authorities.
Founded in 2015 by Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and Anand Prabhudesai, Turtlemint operates an insurance distribution platform that enables insurance agents and advisors to sell policies across categories, including life, health and motor insurance.

AI-powered vendor recovery platform Lawvek has raised $550K in a pre-seed funding round led by Neon Fund, with participation from Inzas Ventures.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its enterprise customer base and strengthen its platform’s ability to identify and recover money owed to businesses by their vendors, Lawvek said in a press release.
Co-founded this year by Amrit Khandelwal and Sudip Chhatui, Lawvek helps enterprises recover vendor overcharges, missed rebates and service credits. It uses AI agents to reconcile contractual terms with invoices, usage data and service records.
The problem stems from enterprises having pricing agreements, discounts and service commitments spread across contracts, billing records and operational data. This makes it difficult to track whether vendors have fulfilled their obligations.
According to McKinsey, unmet supplier commitments can cost large enterprises roughly 2% of their spending. For a company with $1 billion in annual expenditure, this could translate into approximately $20 million in annual losses.
Lawvek’s platform analyses vendor contracts against billing, usage and service records to identify discrepancies. These include price hikes beyond agreed caps, volume discounts missing from invoices and prepaid capacity that businesses may not fully utilise.
When the platform identifies money owed through rebates or service credits, it calculates the amount, collects supporting evidence and submits claims on behalf of customers. It also follows up with vendors and verifies whether the recovery has been reflected in invoices or received as a refund.
The startup is currently helping enterprises in the US identify instances of vendor overpayments and cases where they receive less than what was agreed in their contracts.

Vedachalam, former director of ISRO’s Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre, who contributed to India's cryogenic propulsion programme and several space missions, and Ashutosh Sharma, former secretary of the Department of Science and Technology and Institute Chair Professor at IIT Kanpur.

It also plans to assist portfolio companies with product commercialisation, hiring, business development, access to institutional and enterprise customers, and connections with international markets and follow-on investors.
Through Viksit Bharat Fund-I, CortexSpark Ventures aims to back Indian startups developing proprietary technologies for strategic industries and global markets, with a focus on taking research-led innovations towards commercialisation.

title: Swish spends Rs 145 Cr to generate Rs 48 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
India’s 10-minute food delivery segment has attracted players such as Swish, Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto and Rebel Foods, as companies experiment with freshly prepared meals delivered within minutes. However, the category has seen several setbacks, with Swiggy shutting down Snacc, Zomato pausing Quick, Rebel Foods closing Quickie within a year of launch and Zepto scaling back its Zepto Cafe amid weak demand.
Swish is building its business in this emerging category through an ultra-fast food delivery model and currently operates across five cities. The startup is nearing Rs 50 crore in annual revenue, but its expansion has come with high operating costs, particularly employee expenses, pushing its losses up nearly 5X to Rs 91 crore in FY26.
The Bengaluru-based startup recorded an 11.9X jump in revenue from operations to Rs 47.6 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

Founded in 2024 by Aniket Shah, Ujjwal Sukheja and Saran S., Swish operates a network of neighbourhood cloud kitchens that prepare and deliver fresh meals within 10 minutes. The startup currently has a presence across five cities: Bengaluru, Gurugram, Noida, Delhi and Ghaziabad.
Sale of food products was the company's sole source of operating revenue. It also earned around Rs 6 crore in interest income on bank deposits, taking its total income to Rs 53.75 crore during FY26.
For the food delivery firm, employee benefit expenses emerged as Swish’s largest cost component, accounting for 38.47% of its total expenditure. The company spent Rs 55.7 crore on this head in FY26, against Rs 10.4 crore in FY25, marking a 5.4X increase. Of this, Rs 17.5 crore went towards delivery partner expenses, while the remaining costs covered its workforce.
The cost of materials, which primarily includes ingredients and other inputs required for food preparation, surged 6.9X to Rs 39.5 crore from Rs 5.75 crore in FY25. It accounted for 27.28% of the company's overall expenses.
Marketing and branding emerged as another significant cost head, which rose 9.4X to Rs 19 crore from Rs 2.03 crore in the previous fiscal year. The expense accounted for 13.12% of the total expenditure.
Among other expenses, rent stood at Rs 6.16 crore, while registration, renewals and subscription costs amounted to Rs 4.64 crore. Kitchen operations, housekeeping, professional charges, logistics and other overheads contributed to the overall expense base of Rs 144.8 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.2 crore in FY25.
Amid a sharp rise in employee costs, marketing spends and other operational expenses, Swish’s losses surged 4.8X to Rs 91 crore in FY26 from Rs 19 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Its EBITDA margin and Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stood at -193.2% and -30.9%, respectively.

On a unit level, the Accel-backed startup spent Rs 3.04 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As of March 2026, it had total current assets of Rs 43 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 28 crore.
Swish has raised around $78 million to date, including a recent $24 million round led by Bertelsmann India Investments, with participation from existing investors Accel, Bain Capital Ventures and Hara Global, as exclusively reported by Entrackr. Earlier in March, it raised $38 million in a round led by Hara Global and Bain Capital Ventures.
Backed by fresh funding, Swish is strengthening its kitchen infrastructure and delivery network, while looking to expand into other parts of the country. This is expected to support revenue growth in the coming years, although improving kitchen utilisation, managing delivery costs and building repeat demand will be key to narrowing its losses.

summary:
B2B fintech startup Vegapay is set to raise Rs 38.4 crore or $ 4 million in its Series A funding round, led by Prosus, with participation from existing investors Elevation Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Eximius Ventures.
The board of the Mumbai-based has passed a special resolution to issue  18,090 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 21,221.92 per share to raise the aforesaid amount, according to the documents reviewed by Entrackr.
Prosus, through its investment arm MIH Investments One B.V., will lead the round with an investment of Rs 28.80 crore. Elevation Capital and Vertex Ventures will also participate, investing Rs 6.04 crore and Rs 2.30 crore, respectively. Eximius Ventures will invest the remaining Rs 1.25 crore.
As per Entrackr's estimates, Vegapay's valuation is set to jump 1.76X to around Rs 380 crore in its Series A round, from Rs 216 crore in its pre-Series A round raised just four months ago. However, this appears to be part of a larger funding round, and the valuation may change.
According to its filing in July 2026, the firm had previously raised Rs 37.9 crore (around $4 million) in a pre-Series A round led by Vertex Ventures, which invested Rs 28.42 crore. Elevation Capital and Eximius Ventures also participated in the round with Rs 7.58 crore and Rs 1.90 crore, respectively.
Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal, Puneet Sharma and Abhinav Garg, Vegapay is building a technology stack for digital lending and card management. Its platform enables banks, NBFCs and other financial institutions to launch and manage customised credit products, including credit, debit and prepaid cards, credit lines on UPI, loan origination and collection systems. 
In August 2026, Moneycontrol reported that Vegapay was in talks to raise $15-20 million from Prosus and others.
The firm’s revenue from operations surged 2.8X to Rs 8.74 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 3.10 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, its losses increased marginally to Rs 18.73 crore in FY26 from Rs 18 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Cosine Robots raises Rs 22.36 Cr led by Avaana Capital
summary:
Bengaluru-based deeptech startup Cosine Robots has raised Rs 22.36 crore ($2.4 million) in a funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to set up a dedicated research and development (R&D) and production facility, expand its engineering team and accelerate the development of its integrated servo actuator portfolio.
Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas, Cosine Robots develops actuators and motion systems for robotics applications. Its products combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics and proprietary control software into integrated systems designed to control robotic movement.
The company is developing a common motion architecture through a modular range of cycloidal and planetary actuators. These products are designed for different torque requirements across industrial robotic arms, collaborative robots, quadrupeds and humanoid robots.
Cosine’s technology also includes a proprietary control architecture that combines dual-position sensing with a 25 kHz control loop, enabling 25,000 updates per second. The system is designed to improve precision and control over movement and torque.
The upcoming facility will bring precision machining, assembly, calibration and endurance testing under one roof. The company aims to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities and supply actuators to robot manufacturers in India and overseas.
Avaana Capital invests in deeptech and innovation-led businesses across sectors including advanced manufacturing, AI, robotics, mobility and climate technology. Its portfolio includes Eggoz, Tsuyo Manufacturing, Dreamfly and Kazam.

title: AppsForBharat’s revenue jumps 84% to Rs 129 Cr in FY26
summary:
AppsForBharat, the company behind devotional platform Sri Mandir, reported strong growth in FY26, with its operating revenue surging 84.3% year-on-year to Rs 129 crore from Rs 70 crore in FY25.
The Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue rose 84.3% to Rs 129 crore in FY26 from Rs 70 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


Sri Mandir offers online puja services for devotees unable to visit temples. Priests perform rituals in devotees’ names and gotras, with videos shared afterwards. Sri Mandir launched these services in 2022 with four to five temples and now partners with over 100 temples across India.
AppsForBharat is consolidating operations in temple towns such as Ujjain, Haridwar and Mathura, while expanding its presence in South India.
The company generated Rs 125.62 crore from the sale of services, contributing around 97% of its operating revenue. The remaining Rs 3.3 crore came from the sale of products, accounting for approximately 3% of total revenue.
Including other income, AppsForBharat's total income increased to Rs 141 crore in FY26 from Rs 73 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On the expense front, advertising and promotional expenses remained the largest cost component, rising to Rs 98.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 52 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses increased 78.1% to Rs 57 crore from Rs 32 crore.
Puja and chadhava expenses nearly doubled to Rs 22 crore in FY26 from Rs 11.4 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, tools and technology expenses increased 23.5% to Rs 12.6 crore from Rs 10.2 crore, while other expenses rose 45.2% to Rs 18 crore.
Overall, the company's total expenses increased 76.3% to Rs 208 crore in FY26 from Rs 118 crore in FY25.
Despite revenue growing faster than expenses, the company's net loss widened 49.8% to Rs 67.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 45.26 crore in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, its EBITDA margin improved to -61.05% from -67.76% in FY25, while ROCE stood at -32.64% during the fiscal year.


At a unit level, AppsForBharat spent Rs 1.61 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.69 in the previous fiscal year. Its cash and bank balance declined to Rs 9 crore from Rs 38.5 crore, while current assets stood at Rs 200 crore as of March 2026, against Rs 164 crore a year earlier.
Prashant Sachan, Founder and CEO, said the company continues to invest in its team, AI and initiatives related to temples and priests.
“When we started in 2020, the question was whether families would trust technology with something as personal as their prayers. Six years on, the numbers have answered that, and more devotees than ever can take part in rituals at the temples they hold dear, wherever they are. Our focus now is to strengthen that trust on the ground, by building our presence in temple towns and working with more temples,” said Sachan.
The company raised Rs 175 crore ($20 million) in a Series C round led by Susquehanna Asia Venture Capital in July 2025. It has raised more than $50 million to date and is also backed by Fundamentum, Elevation Capital and Peak XV Partners.

title: Pee Safe’s revenue jumps 54% to Rs 126 Cr in FY26, posts Rs 7 Cr loss
summary:
Personal hygiene and wellness brand Pee Safe reported a 54% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in FY26. However, the company continued to remain in the red during the fiscal year.
Pee Safe’s revenue from operations rose 53.7% to Rs 126 crore in FY26 from Rs 82 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Vikas Bagaria and Srijana Bagaria, Pee Safe offers a range of personal hygiene and wellness products across categories such as menstrual care, intimate hygiene, toilet hygiene, sexual wellness, and grooming. Its product portfolio includes sanitary pads, menstrual cups, tampons, intimate washes, toilet seat sanitizers, lubricants and grooming products.
Revenue from product sales remained the company's sole source of operating revenue, while it generated an additional Rs 1 crore through other income, taking its total income to Rs 127 crore in FY26.
Advertising and promotional expenses, the largest cost component, surged 76.3% to Rs 46 crore in FY26 from Rs 26.09 crore in FY25, accounting for around 34% of total expenses. Cost of materials consumed, another major expense head, increased 59.3% to Rs 43 crore. Employee benefit expenses rose 37.9% to Rs 17.58 crore, while freight costs grew 43.6% to Rs 7.18 crore. Other expenses also increased 29.2% to Rs 20.24 crore.
Overall, Pee Safe’s total expenses increased 54.9% to Rs 134 crore in FY26 from Rs 86.5 crore in FY25.
As expenses grew slightly faster than revenue, Pee Safe's losses jumped 80% to Rs 7.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 4 crore in FY25. Its ROCE stood at -15.36%, while its EBITDA margin was -5.72% during FY26.

On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.06 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Pee Safe’s current assets stood at Rs 77.7 crore, Cash and bank balances jumped 16.8X to Rs 39 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.32 crore in FY25
The Gurugram-based firm has raised around $45 million in funding to date, including a $32 million funding round led by OrbiMed, a global healthcare-focused private equity firm.

The fresh capital towards accelerating digital growth, strengthening brand building and expanding into physical retail, Zavya said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2021 by Poem Kabra and Ravi Malani, Zavya focuses on everyday 925 sterling silver jewellery, combining contemporary designs with a digital-first distribution strategy. The funding comes amid changing jewellery consumption patterns in India, with rising gold prices and evolving consumer preferences driving interest in alternative precious metals. Younger consumers are increasingly exploring hallmarked 925 sterling silver jewellery as a more accessible option for everyday wear, combining precious-metal value with contemporary designs.
While silver jewellery has an established presence in international markets, the category remains relatively underpenetrated in India, particularly across organised and online retail channels, presenting an opportunity for design-led brands.
Zavya sells through its own website and mobile application, quick-commerce platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto, and marketplaces including Amazon, Myntra and Nykaa, where it claims to be among the top brands in its category.

The Mumbai-based firm has crossed Rs 16,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with a combined high-net-worth individual (HNI) and UHNI client base of over 2,900 across more than 12 cities. It has a team of over 100 private bankers and achieved these milestones within two years of operations.
Co-founded by Srikanth Subramanian, Shobhit Mathur and Dharmendra Jain in 2024, Ionic Wealth began operations with an initial investment of around Rs 290 crore from Angel One and marquee families.

All investors from the previous round participated in the latest funding round. These include business families, Bollywood personalities, fintech entrepreneurs, global CXOs, board advisors and media houses, among others.
Ionic Wealth plans to use the fresh capital to scale its HNI business through technology, strengthen global investing capabilities through GIFT City and broaden investment access through the Accredited Investor framework and Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs). It also plans to build a dedicated UHNI proposition for India’s leading families.
Ionic Wealth operates an omnichannel wealth-tech platform focused on HNIs and UHNIs, offering investment opportunities across asset classes, digital wealth management services and customised investment roadmaps. title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 16- Nov 21]
summary:
This week, 23 Indian startups raised $290 million across 6 growth-stage and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw five key appointments, two exits and one fund launch.
In contrast, 12 startups had collectively secured about $31.3 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $290 million across six deals this week. AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest, Nexon Omniverse, the parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore (approximately $52 million) in a Series E funding round. Bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai raised $18 million. 
Robotics company Botsync raised $11 million in a Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures and Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, among others. 
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $147.7 million across 17 deals this week. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt. Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised $24 million in a seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures.
Branded egg company Henfruit raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital. Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Ayra Ventures.
Fatehpuria Hygiene, a trade, supply chain and fulfilment company, raised Rs 100 crore in its maiden equity funding round led by investor Madhu Kela.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding activity with 12 deals during the week, followed by Mumbai and Delhi-NCR with three deals each. Coimbatore, Rajasthan, Pune and Thiruvananthapuram also recorded funding this week.
AI startups led sector-wise funding activity with six deals, followed by e-commerce, semiconductor, FMCG, robotics. Startups across fintech, legal tech, healthtech also raised funds during the week.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led funding activity with five deals, followed by four Series B rounds. Series E, Series A, maiden, debt, pre-Series A and angel also saw activity during the week.
[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding increased nearly 826% to $290 million from $31.3 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $206.9 million across 23 deals.
[Key Hirings]
CarDekho Group appointed Sudhir Pai as CEO of its auto classifieds business and group strategy head.
Medi Assist Healthcare Services appointed Aruna Vaidyanathan, formerly Global Head of Growth Marketing at TCS.
Indian deep-tech company Naxatra Labs has appointed Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as its Chief Product Officer.
[Departures]
Kriti Gupta, vice president at Peak XV Partners, has quit the venture capital firm after five years to join Goodwater Capital.
PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal will step down as Executive Vice Chairman and Whole Time Director on March 31, 2027. He will continue on the company's board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director from April 1, 2027.
[Fund Launches]
Oister Global, an India-focused private markets asset manager, has launched a growth-stage deep tech fund with a target corpus of Rs 400 crore and a greenshoe option of Rs 200 crore, taking its potential size to Rs 600 crore.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Fractal Analytics explores acquisitions of up to 25 AI startups
Fractal Analytics is in discussions with 20–25 AI startups as it looks to expand its capabilities across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering. The company is open to acquisitions worth up to Rs 1,000 crore, with a preferred deal size of $50 million to $100 million.
▪️ OpenAI appoints Pragya Misra to lead business development in India and South Asia
OpenAI's India head of strategy and global affairs, Pragya Misra, is moving into a new role to lead business development across India and South Asia. She joined OpenAI in 2024 as its first employee in India.
▪️ CarDekho Group appoints former Magicbricks CEO Sudhir Pai
CarDekho Group has appointed Sudhir Pai as CEO of its auto classifieds business and Group Strategy Head. He will oversee platforms including CarDekho.com, ZigWheels and BikeDekho.
▪️ PhonePe partners with Kerala Startup Mission to support startups
PhonePe has partnered with Kerala Startup Mission to support startups through digital payment infrastructure, onboarding assistance and technical support. The partnership will also include workshops and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
▪️ Drip Capital signs Rs 5,000 Cr trade finance pact with Bihar government
Drip Capital has signed an MoU with Bihar's Department of Industries to facilitate up to Rs 5,000 crore in trade finance for MSME exporters over five years. The partnership will provide collateral-free working capital and connect local manufacturers with domestic and international buyers.
▪️ Rediff files updated draft papers for Rs 600 Cr IPO
Rediff.com India has filed updated draft IPO papers proposing a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 600 crore, without an offer-for-sale component. The company operates consumer internet and enterprise communication businesses.
